bug_semantics: For an Iceberg connector using a REST catalog, the table FileIO property map can contain static object-store access keys or temporary credentials vended by the catalog. Trino copied that complete secret-bearing map into JSON-serializable IcebergWritableTableHandle and IcebergTableExecuteHandle objects embedded in the serialized query plan. A user with SQL write or table-maintenance privilege could submit such an operation and retrieve their own query JSON through the UI, /ui/api/query/<query_id>, or /v1/query/<query_id>, exposing the catalog's storage credentials.
flaw_origin: Commit 97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23 implemented Iceberg REST vended-S3 access by adding a fileIoProperties map populated from table.io().properties() to IcebergWritableTableHandle and IcebergTableExecuteHandle, exposing it as a JSON property so workers could reconstruct a credentialed filesystem. This placed secrets in plan handles rather than transporting them through a separate credential channel; the exact fields and JSON accessors do not exist in direct parent 28c3c1172d331962eda6aa1066b419127a9b9668.
ai_marker: absent — the exact raw BIC commit object names human author Alex Jo <jo.alex2144@gmail.com> and human committer David Phillips <david@acz.org>; its message is only "Support vended s3 credentials in the Iceberg REST catalog" and contains no trailers, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool marker, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/trinodb/trino/security/advisories/GHSA-x27p-5f68-m644 states that static or vended Iceberg REST storage credentials were stored in write/procedure handles serialized into query JSON, reachable by the submitting user through the UI and /ui/api/query/<query_id> or /v1/query/<query_id>; it defines affected versions [439,480) and patched version 480.

BIC page https://github.com/trinodb/trino/commit/97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23 and local patch inspection show that 97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23 added Map<String,String> fileIoProperties, its @JsonCreator parameter, and @JsonProperty getter to plugin/trino-iceberg/src/main/java/io/trino/plugin/iceberg/IcebergWritableTableHandle.java, and added the same secret-bearing field/property to plugin/trino-iceberg/src/main/java/io/trino/plugin/iceberg/procedure/IcebergTableExecuteHandle.java. In plugin/trino-iceberg/src/main/java/io/trino/plugin/iceberg/IcebergMetadata.java it populated those values with table.io().properties() for writes and maintenance procedures.

Smallest-origin proof: `git log --all --reverse -SfileIoProperties --` over IcebergWritableTableHandle.java, IcebergMetadata.java, IcebergPageSinkProvider.java, and IcebergTableExecuteHandle.java returns 97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23 as the first relevant commit; `git log -L 44,44:plugin/trino-iceberg/src/main/java/io/trino/plugin/iceberg/IcebergWritableTableHandle.java 97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23` attributes the first field line directly to that commit. It is a one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, or merge aggregate.

Direct-parent verification: `git diff 28c3c1172d331962eda6aa1066b419127a9b9668 97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23 --` shows both handle fields, constructor parameters, assignments, and JSON getters as additions from /dev/null hunks relative to the direct parent. Thus the vulnerable secret-bearing handle members are absent from the parent tree.

Version-boundary proof from the validated clone: tags resolve to 438=bc85d90ae640e9c29c909858a2a93992d07e8d2e, 439=089d8afb97086c59638ed2956913b869869c9661, 479=1b3a3e39a657642b0c4f76a5439dae859f93b4b1, and 480=0ace945c7bbffa0d89b18cbae09151f4ae293c30. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the BIC is not in 438 but is in 439, 479, and 480, matching the advisory's first-affected boundary. First-party release page: https://github.com/trinodb/trino/releases/tag/439.

Direct remediation https://github.com/trinodb/trino/commit/d82519245e82fa23a6ea608e99417a566ae52cff removes fileIoProperties from both JSON-plan handles, introduces io.trino.spi.connector.ConnectorTableCredentials and IcebergTableCredentials, obtains the credentials separately from connector metadata, and passes them by PlanNodeId through TaskUpdateRequest to page source/sink providers. This preserves worker access while keeping credentials out of the serialized plan that query JSON exposes.

Fixed-boundary proof: `git merge-base --is-ancestor d82519245e82fa23a6ea608e99417a566ae52cff 479` is false and the same check against 480 is true. `git diff 479 480 -- plugin/trino-iceberg/src/main/java/io/trino/plugin/iceberg/IcebergWritableTableHandle.java plugin/trino-iceberg/src/main/java/io/trino/plugin/iceberg/procedure/IcebergTableExecuteHandle.java` shows removal of the fileIoProperties record components and assignments. First-party release pages are https://github.com/trinodb/trino/releases/tag/479 and https://github.com/trinodb/trino/releases/tag/480.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit 97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23` yields tree b9a6aefed17e6cc610234a3da3238bab8c6b4265, parent 28c3c1172d331962eda6aa1066b419127a9b9668, author Alex Jo <jo.alex2144@gmail.com>, committer David Phillips <david@acz.org>, and only the subject "Support vended s3 credentials in the Iceberg REST catalog"; no AI marker or trailer is present.
reasoning: The advisory's attack path points to secrets residing in serialized write and table-procedure handles, so the causal search followed the secret-bearing fileIoProperties member rather than later credential-refresh code. Pickaxe and line history identify 97308450703c0de91da501f3571876b908a5bf23 as the first commit to copy table.io().properties() into JSON-visible Iceberg handles. Its immediate-parent diff proves those exact vulnerable members were absent before it, and tag ancestry places the change precisely between releases 438 and 439, consistent with the first affected version. Later record conversions and refactors retained the same member and therefore are not BICs. The direct fix d82519245e82fa23a6ea608e99417a566ae52cff removes credentials from plan handles and creates a separate ConnectorTableCredentials transport to workers; it is absent from 479 and present in patched release 480. Finally, the raw BIC commit object contains only human author/committer identities and no AI-related trailer or marker. Under BIC-only attribution, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
